login: replace scoped_ptr with std::unique_ptr scoped_ptr has been deprecated and removed from chrome/base in favor of std::unique_ptr from C++11. libchrome currently maintains a local patch that simply aliases scoped_ptr as std::unique_ptr. arc-networkd: Implement privilege separation for ArcIpConfig ArcIpConfig requires CAP_SYS_ADMIN, CAP_NET_ADMIN, and CAP_DAC_READ_SEARCH, the most dangerous capabilities used by the daemon. Fork a helper subprocess to handle changing the IP configuration and manipulating the namespace, and then let Manager drop privileges before it starts handling dbus/ndp/multicast duties. Manager will still run with CAP_NET_RAW, as an unprivileged user. Future work may involve splitting NDP handling into a less-privileged subprocess to limit the extent of damage if it is subverted. The new HelperProcess class can be used for additional subprocesses. BUG=chromium:670985 TEST=manually verify IPv6/multicast functionality TEST=manually verify creds via /proc/<pid>/status TEST=`kill -11` the main/sub processes and ensure that both die CQ-DEPEND=CL:416377,CL:416256 Change-Id: I2ddec4ffbf516b583762b0405909a14088552fe1 Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/416361 Commit-Ready: Kevin Cernekee <cernekee@chromium.org> Tested-by: Kevin Cernekee <cernekee@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Mattias Nissler <mnissler@chromium.org>

UPSTREAM: USB: core: let USB device know device node Although most of USB devices are hot-plug's, there are still some devices are hard wired on the board, eg, for HSIC and SSIC interface USB devices. If these kinds of USB devices are multiple functions, and they can supply other interfaces like i2c, gpios for other devices, we may need to describe these at device tree. In this commit, it uses "reg" in dts as physical port number to match the phyiscal port number decided by USB core, if they are the same, then the device node is for the device we are creating for USB core. util: Add a new utility 'vpd_get_value' that speeds up value reading. There may be more and more upstart jobs (or scripts) need to fetch VPD values. In comparison to the huge dump_vpd_log, which was solely designed for creating the cache (and full-report), many scripts simply want to read one single value and needs an optimized version of utility helping to read from VPD, no matter if it's from /sys (available on recent devices) or legacy cache. This script tries to optimize and hide all logic so it should be the fastest way to read one single VPD entry. UPSTREAM: xfrm: fix crash in XFRM_MSG_GETSA netlink handler If we hit any of the error conditions inside xfrm_dump_sa(), then xfrm_state_walk_init() never gets called. However, we still call xfrm_state_walk_done() from xfrm_dump_sa_done(), which will crash because the state walk was never initialized properly. We can fix this by setting cb->args[0] only after we've processed the first element and checking this before calling xfrm_state_walk_done(). init: add delayed installation script and document During the reimaging stage, the DUT downloads a test image and a factory toolkit to the local storage. The DUT is responsible for installing the toolkit itself afterward. But in that stage, the DUT (running factory shim or factory netboot installer) lacks of `python` to finish essential works for installing the factory toolkit. It can only extract the toolkit file but not install. We have to delay this work until the first boot using test image environment. BUG=b:33094336 TEST=Manually tested: 1. Flash a DUT to test image (no factory toolkit installed) 2. Copy the `init` folder to `/usr/local/factory/init` on the DUT 3. Copy factory toolkit to `/usr/local/factory` on the DUT 4. `echo "/usr/local/factory/install_factory_toolkit.run" >/usr/local/factory/init/install` 5. Reboot the DUT, saw it installs the factory toolkit and invokes factory software Change-Id: I89e0d7ca037f3905115fb5e76c6046a44691e4a4 Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/417640 Commit-Ready: Mao Huang <littlecvr@chromium.org> Tested-by: Mao Huang <littlecvr@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Hung-Te Lin <hungte@chromium.org>

CHROMIUM: tpm: Send Shutdown command for TPM2 during shutdown TPM 2.0 chips detect an unorderly shutdown, which may trigger defense mechanisms, if TPM2_Startup is not immediately preceded by TPM2_Shutdown. Send TPM2_Shutdown(CLEAR) during shutdown for TPM 2.0 chips to prevent this situation. The command is sent from the already existing hook registered through register_reboot_notifier() rather than from the shutdown handler in driver. The reason for that is that such hooks are called before the shutdown handler, and the existing hook prevents any commands from being sent to TPM after it (for "gentle shutdown" purposes). BUG=chrome-os-partner:60653 TEST=Boot Chrome OS on a device with TPM 2.0 running Cr50, check dictionary_attack_counter using 'tpm_manager_client status', reboot, check dictionary_attack_counter again. It shouldn't increase. Change-Id: If98f439998d4c0916e49437f9735826288eef1be Signed-off-by: Andrey Pronin <apronin@chromium.org> Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/418220 Reviewed-by: Luigi Semenzato <semenzato@chromium.org>
